column1: Validation target was main HEAD 3cc63c55ed04df7035c1c06a8cc754e20a0b1ce1, not current working-tree source. Method: read staging CHANNEL_GRAPH.md, then enumerate production handler source through git show main:<file>; tests and docs were not counted as runtime readers or writers. Direct stack writes, produced_channels/producers, direct stack.get reads, and stack helper reads such as _stack_attr(stack, ...), _stack_value(stack, ...), and _array_or_none(stack, ...) were counted. Result: most staging claims stay directionally valid, but several are not literal orphan channels. corruption_map is still a real orphan write: biome_channels writes and declares it, but no production stack reader consumes it. forest_mask, material_zones, and legacy water_depth are still read-orphans. The four structural labels are not literal orphans because terrain_labels writes and declares them, but staging is correct that the writer is only a validator/preserver that zero-fills when no upstream generator stamped real masks. That makes their consumer chain semantically broken, not absent. water_surface_mask, water_surface_elevation_m, and water_depth_m are wired on main. Their reader sets have moved since the staging graph, and several consumers still read them without matching consumed_channels declarations. Spec names water_surface_z, shoreline_mask, wet_fetch, flow_velocity_xy, foam_potential, waterfall_mask, wave_fetch, and wet_zone_override are absent from production stack use; these are spec/code vocabulary gaps, not runtime orphan reads. weathering_timeline is not a stack channel at all; it is a source tag/function area that mutates wetness and should be tracked under wetness ownership/override rules. New orphan surfaced outside the staging orphan list: height_m. pass_water_depth reads and declares height_m, but main has no stack writer for height_m; it falls back to height, so height_m should be optional or removed from consumed_channels unless a real producer is added. Biggest declaration risk is scheduling, not just documentation: optional helper reads are invisible to PassDAG. Fix order should prioritize water_depth migration, label stamping, forest/material producers, then declaration cleanup before relying on graph-driven validation gates in CI or PR review now.
